subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC - Data isolation expectations
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@finsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)

Hi Alice — thanks again for your time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and the items we discussed so we can align next steps.

Key takeaways from the call:
- FinSecure handles regulated financial data and has strict isolation requirements (PCI scope for parts of the workload, long-term retention controls).
- Primary goal: ensure model inference does not expose raw customer data to multi-tenant inference pools or external tenants.
- Shortlist of deployment options we discussed: Hosted API (not preferred for regulated data), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity), Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem private control plane).

Questions / clarifications needed from your side:
1) Can you confirm whether all inference traffic must stay inside your VPC (no egress to public networks)?
2) Do you require customer-managed KMS/HSM for encryption keys?
3) Expected steady-state throughput (req/s) and concurrency for the PoC?
4) Compliance artifacts you want up front (SOC 2 attestation, architecture diagrams, data flow)?

Initial recommendations based on what you said:
- For full regulatory isolation and control over network egress + KMS: Private VPC or on-prem deployment is the recommended long-term approach.
- For fast time-to-value and to validate integration: a Dedicated capacity deployment with private peering and strict routing can sometimes be used as an interim step if we can meet your network/KMS requirements (we can restrict tenancy and disable model-sharing telemetry).

Attachments: I attached a brief Private vs Dedicated comparison and our most recent SOC 2 snapshot for your security team.

Proposed next steps:
- You share answers to the 4 clarifying Qs above and the security questionnaire (attached).
- If you’re open, we schedule a technical deep-dive next week (Redwood infra + your network/security engineer).
- We’ll put together a simple mutual action plan (timeline, PoC success criteria, cost estimate) once we confirm throughput and KMS/peering constraints.

I copied Marissa (solutions) so she can help set up the deep dive and draft the MAP.

Thanks —
Mateo
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Alice Chen <alice@finsecure.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, security@finsecure.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)

Thanks, Mateo — appreciate the clear recap. A few answers and context from our side:

Answers to your Qs:
1) Yes — inference traffic must terminate inside our VPC. No pingbacks to public inference pools; we need private peering or an on-prem connector.
2) We require customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS). Keys must be under our control; Redwood should support wrapping/unwrapping with our key.
3) Expected PoC load: ~75–120 requests/sec peak, average ~30 req/s. Latency SLO for user-facing features is 200–300ms p50.
4) Security artifacts needed up front: SOC2 attestation, architecture diagram showing network flow, and data retention/audit log details.

Preference & constraints:
- Our security/compliance team prefers Private VPC or on-prem for full rollout. That said, we’d consider starting with Dedicated (reserved capacity) if you can guarantee: no multi-tenant mixing, traffic stays on our peered network, and KMS integration with our AWS account. We’d need to see contractual SLAs and an architectural diagram for that approach.

I’ve attached our security questionnaire — hope that helps scope the deep dive. We’re targeting a decision by the end of May.

Next steps from FinSecure: we’ll review the SOC2 snapshot you sent and fill in the questionnaire; I’ll follow up with our infra lead if we want to schedule the deep dive.

—
Alice Chen
Head of Security & Compliance | FinSecure
alice@finsecure.com

Hi Alice — great, thank you for the clear answers. Quick follow-up and a proposed plan so we can keep momentum: 

Short answers:
- Private VPC is the recommended final architecture to meet the requirements you described (VPC-local inference, customer-managed AWS KMS, audit logs retained per your retention policy).
- Dedicated can be used as a staged approach for a PoC if we sign a short-term carve-out: private peering, dedicated tenancy, KMS forwarding to your AWS account, and contractual guarantees on no multi-tenant access. We will provide an architecture diagram and an SLA addendum for that path.

Proposed immediate next steps (I’ll own coordination):
1) Technical deep-dive (60–90m) with your infra/security + our infra and product engineering — proposed slots: Wed 4/14 10am-12pm PT or Thu 4/15 2pm-4pm PT. Marissa will send a calendar invite once you confirm a slot.
2) We’ll return: (a) an architecture diagram for Dedicated-with-peering and (b) a Private VPC network diagram showing egress controls and KMS flow.
3) I’ll upload our SOC2 package and a short MAP to the HubSpot deal and share links here (estimated cost range for PoC + 3-month Dedicated run vs Private VPC baseline).
4) You fill and return the security questionnaire; we’ll have our security team answer any follow-ups directly.

Attachments/Links I’ll send after the call: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (draft), SOC2 bundle (redwood-soc2-2026.zip), architecture diagrams. For now I’ve added the HubSpot deal link and the MAP link above.

If you prefer, we can prepare a price comparison for the two options (Dedicated PoC -> Private VPC migration) so Procurement can see the delta.

Thanks again — looking forward to the deep dive.
Mateo
